passages.original: Septuaginta autem interpretes, secundum quos ista tractamus, qui posuerunt gaeson, miror si et in graeca lingua hastam uel lanceam gallicanam intellegi uoluerunt: ea quippe dicuntur gaesa, quorum et Uergilius meminit, ubi ait de Gallis in scuto Aeneae pictis: duo quisque Alpina coruscant gaesa manu.
passages.english: But as for the Seventy translators, according to whom we are treating these things, who put *gaeson*, I wonder whether in the Greek language too they meant a Gallic spear or lance to be understood. For those are called *gaesa* which Virgil also mentions, where he says of the Gauls depicted on the shield of Aeneas: "each brandishes two Alpine / javelins in his hand."
passages.notes: *Gaeson*/*gaesa*: a heavy throwing-spear of Gallic type. The quotation is from Virgil, Aeneid 8.661–662.
